notes: OpenCode 2.x through the service API (#2109 P5b-1). The parent's task-tool child runs a shell `sleep 30`; inside the maintainer-approved service window the service — the only process either session has — is SIGKILLed. The daemon reports the service pid exited for the child and the parent; the orphan never goes working during cleanup.

text: The parent API session is admitted on its first activity
The session binds to the one running 2.x service (pid.go servicePIDFor) — there is no client process
The prompt drives the parent to working
The task tool's child session is admitted: a NEW ses_… transcript_new
The child is linked to the parent

The SIGKILLed service takes the orphaned child with it: process_exited for the child. The invariants are a lock — after that exit the child is never re-admitted to working or waiting (the daemon deletes it there); the DSL scans only events after the matched one, so they do not cover the kill-to-exit window
The same exit reaps the parent: process_exited for the parent session
